key_insight: The paper shows how to map classical model weights into low-dimensional quantum circuits via subspace selection, unitary projection, and Lie-algebraic generator extraction to enable zero-shot quantum learning and reduce barren-plateau risk.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical warm-start and model-merging strategy for parameterized quantum circuits that can improve trainability without requiring costly quantum-side optimization.
method: Select a k-dimensional subspace with Stiefel geometry to compress classical parameters.
Project the resulting operator to the nearest unitary, then extract a logarithmic generator for quantum evolution.
Use identity-centered architectures to keep generators near the identity and avoid log branch-cut issues.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an IBM ibm_kobe experiment achieving Hellinger fidelity of 0.987 at k=8, with resolvable subspace gradients up to 128 physical qubits.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate subspace selection and near-unitary behavior, so performance may degrade if the learned operator is far from unitary or the logarithm becomes numerically unstable.
paper_title: Lie-Algebraic Subspace Quantization for Zero-Shot Quantum Learning and Barren-Plateau Mitigation
